speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a neck swelling; how long has it been present, and have you noticed any changes in its size, color, or texture? Do you experience pain, difficulty swallowing, or any changes in your voice?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Neck (Secondary to Head and Neck Primary, likely undiagnosed or previously treated, with distant history of Colon Cancer).

Wait, I need to clarify the timeline. You mentioned colon cancer at age 43; was the neck swelling present before or after that surgery? Also, have you ever had any skin lesions, ulcers, or masses on your face or scalp?
